records.section_heading: Background on COTs (life history and ecology)
records.question: According to the section, how long after heavy rain or storm events are Crown of Thorns outbreaks likely to occur?
records.ground_truth_answer: Approximately three years after heavy rain or storm events.
ground_truth_chunks: When large storms bring heavy rains these nutrients are washed into the ocean, leading to an increase in phytoplankton, a marine plant which serves as a food source for larval COTs (Lucas, 1982).
Outbreaks are likely to occur approximately three years after heavy rain or storm events as it takes three years for COTs to mature (Lucas, 1984).

records.question: How was the intensity of COT outbreaks recorded during the towed snorkeler surveys and what criteria defined each category?
records.ground_truth_answer: Intensity was recorded as light, medium, or heavy. Light: a few COTs or scars spaced out along the reef but no areas with overlapping COT scars; Medium: patches of multiple COT scars in an area, with breaks of healthy coral between patches; Heavy: COT scars overlapping to form a continuous area of COTs scars along the reef with no break between scars.
ground_truth_chunks: Intensity was recorded as light (A few COTs or scars spaced out along the reef but no areas with overlapping COT scars), medium (patches of multiple COT scars in an area, with breaks of healthy coral between patches), or heavy (COT scars overlapping to form a continuous area of COTs scars along the reef with no break between scars).

records.question: What size range was estimated to correspond to 2-3 years for individual COTs?
ground_truth_chunks: Age was estimated as between 1 and 2 years for 30- 100 mm individuals, 2-3 years for 100-250 mm individuals, 3-4 years for 250-300 mm individuals, 4-5 years for 300-400 mm individuals, and 5+ year for starfish over 380 mm (Hughes et al., 2014).

records.question: How many COTs were killed between March 2013 and October 2014?
records.ground_truth_answer: A total of 15,537 COTs were killed between March 2013 and October 2014.
ground_truth_chunks: A total of 15,537 COTs were killed between March 2013 and October 2014 during 619 eradication dives (Fig. 3 & 4).
Of these, 6849 were located in park waters (329 dives) and 8688 were outside of the park (290 dives) (Table 1 & 2).

records.question: According to the Discussion, what eradication treatment increased diver efficiency and eliminated the need to handle crown-of-thorns starfish (COTs)?
ground_truth_chunks: Use of oxbile has greatly increased the efficiency of divers, and eliminated the need to handle COTs during eradication efforts.
Oxbile requires a single injection, eliminating the time needed to pull the animal from the reef.
